source_caption_text:
BREAKING🚨 A Sacramento cop SMILED over a handcuffed 66-year-old woman. She never woke up. Now the city has approved $1.4 MILLION for her daughter.

Koya had been sleeping in her car in a parking lot at Haggin Oaks Golf Course after it broke down. When Officer Matthew Sterling answered a trespassing call on November 17, 2024, she told him her phone had died and asked to use his to call her daughter or a cab. He said no. He told her he could take her to a homeless shelter or to jail.

"I'm gonna tell you what I'm gonna do now because I got to a point I don't care anymore," Sterling says in the body camera footage, which just came out through the family's lawsuit.

He pulled her out of the car in her bathrobe, forced her face down on the pavement, put his knee on her back and handcuffed her. As he held her beside his patrol car, her head rolled back and she lost consciousness. 

Paramedics found no pulse. She never woke up and died about a week later. Two images in the lawsuit show Sterling smiling widely as he kneels over her.

The county coroner ruled her death natural, caused by a blood clot that traveled to her lungs. The city says whether police caused her death is still "very much in dispute." The City Council approved the $1.4 million in a closed-door meeting on November 10. The city says the deal is not final yet. The family's attorney says the amount will not change.

Sterling is STILL a Sacramento police officer. In 2025 he earned $226,528, including $129,200 in overtime. The city has not said whether he was ever disciplined.

"She deserved respect," her daughter, Nathifa Wright, told the Sacramento Bee. "Not to be treated like a dog on the street."

"She was my world," Wright said.
